data.title: Heavy rain floods Kanchanaburi, leaves two missing and 400 households evacuated
data.description: KANCHANABURI — Heavy rain has triggered widespread flooding across this western province, forcing more than 400 households to evacuate, disrupting power and communications and leaving a mother and daughter missing after their pickup truck was swept away by floodwaters.

data.title: Thai Airways cancels 8 more flights amid luggage chaos
data.description: Thai Airways International has cancelled eight more flights on routes between Bangkok and Khon Kaen, Phuket, Hanoi and Singapore amid the baggage handling chaos at Suvarnabhumi airport.

data.title: Mae Klong Dam boosts discharge as flood-hit provinces remain inundated
data.description: KANCHANABURI — Communities living downstream of the Mae Klong Dam face imminent flooding as the dam increases water discharges to prevent it from reaching capacity.

data.title: Malaysia begins sending home Myanmar refugees despite safety concerns
data.description: LUMUT, Malaysia - Malaysia began the process of deporting around 1,500 Myanmar nationals on Tuesday as part of a refugee repatriation programme, defying objections from the United Nations and dozens of human rights groups.

data.title: Vietnam arrests three on terrorism charges, including Norwegian and Australian citizens
data.description: HO CHI MINH — Vietnam police have ⁠arrested ⁠three people, including a Norwegian ​citizen and an Australian national of Vietnamese origin, accusing them of terrorism, in ​an operation that a pro-democracy group says ‌was conducted in Cambodia.

data.title: Irish Film Festival returns for 8th edition
data.description: The Embassy of Ireland in Thailand is hosting the Irish Film Festival, with 2026 marking the 8th edition of the festival in Thailand.

data.title: Twenty roads still flooded in Bangkok
data.description: At least 20 roads in the capital were still under water, with flood levels ranging from 10cm to 30.8cm on Tuesday morning, the city's drainage and sewerage department reported.

data.title: IRPC receives Gold Human Rights Award for third consecutive year
data.description: IRPC Plc led by Therdkiat Prommoon, Chief Executive Officer and President, received a plaque of recognition and a certificate for the 2026 Human Rights Model Organisation Award at the Gold level from the Ministry of Justice’s Department of Rights and Liberties Protection.

data.title: 8.3 million refugees at risk due to 'severe' funding cuts: UN
data.description: GENEVA - Nearly 8.3 million refugees and other forcibly displaced people face losing vital assistance from the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR), the UN's refugee agency warned Tuesday, as protection services crumble due to "severe" funding cuts.

data.title: Manchester City's Premier League charges: What comes next?
data.description: MANCHESTER (UNITED KINGDOM) - Manchester City's fate in a legal battle with the Premier League is yet to be sealed, but reports they have been found guilty on widespread financial misconduct has sparked speculation of what comes next.

data.title: Central Tokyo records 34 consecutive days of rain, longest on record
data.description: Central Tokyo on Tuesday registered 34 consecutive days of rain, marking the longest streak on record, according to the weather agency.

data.title: Commerce Ministry moves to help ease shortages
data.description: Commerce Minister Suphajee Suthumpun has ordered the ministry to closely monitor supplies and prices in flood-affected areas and coordinate deliveries to communities where flooding has disrupted transport.

data.title: Decoding ‘medical innovation’: driving Thailand’s economy and transforming healthcare
data.description: Amid the dual pressures of a rapidly ageing society and a sharp rise in non-communicable diseases (NCDs), Thailand faces a critical challenge: optimising public healthcare budgets to ensure all citizens have equal, life-saving access to modern medical care. A high-level multi-stakeholder policy dialogue titled “Advancing Thailand’s Medical Economy through Health Innovation,” was convened in Bangkok by the US-Asean Business Council in early September this year, marked a significant milestone in shaping the country’s healthcare economy through international collaboration. Attended by officials from the US Embassy, health economics experts, healthcare professionals and global life sciences leaders, the forum outlined a vision to transform the nation’s healthcare landscape in the long term.

data.title: Celine Dion wows Paris Fashion Week with surprise gig
data.description: PARIS - Celine Dion kicked off Paris Fashion Week in style on Monday, stepping onto the catwalk beneath the Eiffel Tower and belting out "I'm Alive" to a delighted crowd in a surprise performance.

data.title: Brazil's cellphone crime: a security nightmare in every pocket
data.description: RIO DE JANEIRO - Eduardo Metzker, 29, was riding his motorcycle in Rio de Janeiro when he was suddenly boxed in by two other bikes. One of the riders put a gun to his head and demanded his phone and passcode.

data.title: Italy rebound in Turkey as France win late in Belgium
data.description: PARIS - Italy crushed Turkey 4-1 in the Bursa rain to drag themselves into contention in Nations League Group A1, as leaders France struck late to win 1-0 in Belgium on Monday.

data.title: A new Asean dictionary awaits  at 'A-Z Of Southeast Asian Art'
data.description: Established by the Creador Foundation, Muara Arts -- a new non-profit institution dedicated to Southeast Asian contemporary art -- will launch in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia, on Nov 1 with its inaugural exhibition "A-Z Of Southeast Asian Art: A Critical Dictionary".

data.title: Rethinking stroke care
data.description: According to the Ministry of Public Health, the number of stroke patients treated in public hospitals has been continually increasing: approximately 135,600 in 2023, 146,300 in 2024 and 162,000 in 2025.

data.title: Hospital battles rising waters
data.description: Rayong: Flooding in Klaeng district worsened on Monday after water from the Prasae River inundated low-lying areas and Klaeng Hospital, disrupting operations and cutting off normal food and supply deliveries.

data.title: War Elephants eye revenge on Vietnam
data.description: Revenge is on the menu in Bandung Tuesday night as the War Elephants, with wounded pride to restore, come face to face with Vietnam again, the side that beat them in the Asean Hyundai Cup final.

data.title: Cabinet backs B497m AI-powered weather scheme
data.description: The cabinet has approved a 497-million-baht project for fiscal 2027 to bring satellite and AI-powered weather forecasting from US climate technology company Tomorrow.io to the Thai Meteorological Department.

data.description: The government has instructed all agencies to prepare medical personnel, medicines, and mobile medical teams to assist in flood-affected areas, said Public Health permanent secretary Somreuk Juengsamarn.
